hero.subtitle: A free live webinar for adoptive and foster parents who are tired of the yelling, the power struggles, and the guilt, and ready to understand what their child's anger is really trying to say.
hero.paragraph1: In this engaging and practical webinar, foster and adoptive parent expert and adoptee psychotherapist Jeanette Yoffe, M.A., LMFT, will help parents understand the hidden messages beneath anger and learn attachment-based strategies that build connection rather than conflict.
hero.paragraph2: Participants will discover how early trauma, separation, and attachment disruptions impact a child's developing brain and nervous system, often causing children to react.

countdown.heading: The live session begins in
countdown.live: We're live now. Come on in.
countdown.ended: This session has ended. Register to get the replay.

forYou.heading: This is for you if...
items: Your child's anger can go from zero to a hundred in seconds, and you never see it coming.
Time-outs, rewards, and consequences just aren't working anymore.
You love your child deeply, but some days you feel like you're walking on eggshells.
You want connection instead of conflict, but you're not sure how to get there.

learn.heading: What you'll walk away with
items: The hidden messages underneath your child's anger, and what they're really asking for.
How early trauma, separation, and attachment disruptions shape a child's brain and nervous system.
Attachment-based strategies that build connection instead of escalating conflict.
What to do in the heat of the moment so it doesn't become a battle.

guide.name: Jeanette Yoffe, M.A., LMFT
guide.bio: Jeanette Yoffe, M.A., LMFT, is a foster and adoptive parent expert and an adoptee psychotherapist. She has dedicated her career to helping families understand attachment and trauma, and to turning conflict into connection through compassionate, attachment-based care.

trust.heading: Why families trust this webinar
trust.audience: Join adoptive and foster families from across California, supported by the Fear to Love methodology and the Love Pathways Wraparound team.
